title: Study Microstructural of CoCrFeMnNi High-entropy Alloys Modified with V and Mo
content: The first high entropy alloy HEA proposed was the equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi system with a single-phase FCC structure [1]. The CrMnFeCoNi HEA is interesting because it is ductile but exhibits relatively low strength. For this reason, it is necessary to incorporate other elements to improve the strength by forming a multiphase alloy with crystalline structures of a smaller number of slip systems [2]. Mechanical alloying by high-energy ball milling (HEBM) is a synthesis process of great interest to the scientific community and at an industrial level due to its easy operation and the possibility of industrial scaling [3]. Some advantages of HEBM to obtain HEAs are room temperature processing, grain refinement, high microstructural and chemical homogeneity, stabilization of metastable phases, high concentration of structural defects and lattice distortions [4], which have been reported to improve the mechanical properties of HEAs [5]. For this reason, HEBM is of special interest in enhancing the strength of CrMnFeCoNi HEA. However, the effects of different alloying elements on the structure and microstructure of alloyed powders have been barely studied [6]. Thus, this study used Mo and V as alloying elements in CrMnFeCoNi HEA due to their significant improvement in mechanical properties compared to other elements [7].
